evidence.claim: Article 104 vests executive authority in the President, including national-security policy, treaty ratification, appointment and dismissal of ministers and senior officials, military-use decisions, and presidential decrees subject to legal limits; Article 116 lets the TBMM or the President renew elections; Article 105 sets a parliamentary investigation path.
evidence.title: Anayasa | Anayasa Mahkemesi
evidence.excerpt: Article 104 vests executive authority in the President, including national-security policy, treaty ratification, appointment and dismissal of ministers and senior officials, military-use decisions, and presidential decrees subject to legal limits; Article 116 lets the TBMM or the President renew elections; Article 105 sets a parliamentary investigation path.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary constitutional text governing the 2022 presidency; direct and stable legal authority/constraint source.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Defines Erdoğan's office-level authority and checks in 2022; not a claim about personal conduct.
contrary_evidence: The same articles constrain decree power and preserve parliamentary/judicial checks.
Formal authority does not prove how he used it in practice.

evidence.claim: The Black Sea Grain Initiative was launched in Istanbul by the Russian Federation, Türkiye, Ukraine and the United Nations on 22 July 2022 to enable safe transport of grain and reduce global hunger and food insecurity.
evidence.title: Black Sea Grain Initiative Frequently Asked Questions
evidence.excerpt: The Black Sea Grain Initiative was launched in Istanbul by the Russian Federation, Türkiye, Ukraine and the United Nations on 22 July 2022 to enable safe transport of grain and reduce global hunger and food insecurity.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UN explanatory page on the initiative's creation, purpose, and structure.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Erdoğan's government as host and participant, but implementation was multilateral.
contrary_evidence: This is a humanitarian and logistical initiative, not a treaty settlement or ceasefire.
It shows mediation capacity more than broad peace leadership across all conflicts.

evidence.claim: Erdoğan, Niinistö and Andersson agreed a trilateral memorandum addressing Türkiye's legitimate security concerns, paving the way for Finland and Sweden's NATO membership.
evidence.title: Türkiye, Finland, and Sweden sign agreement paving the way for Finnish and Swedish NATO membership
evidence.excerpt: Erdoğan, Niinistö and Andersson agreed a trilateral memorandum addressing Türkiye's legitimate security concerns, paving the way for Finland and Sweden's NATO membership.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary NATO statement on the agreement and its diplomatic significance.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Erdoğan as a participating head of government in the negotiations.
contrary_evidence: This is alliance bargaining, not a pure peace settlement.
Turkey used veto leverage, so the move was cooperative but also coercive.

evidence.claim: IMF staff said late-2021 rate cuts added vulnerabilities and recommended early policy-rate hikes, stronger central-bank independence, tight fiscal policy, and targeted assistance to vulnerable households.
evidence.title: IMF Staff Completes 2022 Article IV Mission to Türkiye
evidence.excerpt: IMF staff said late-2021 rate cuts added vulnerabilities and recommended early policy-rate hikes, stronger central-bank independence, tight fiscal policy, and targeted assistance to vulnerable households.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: IMF end-of-mission statement is a primary institutional assessment of the 2022 policy mix and its recommended correction.
evidence.period_fit: Directly addresses the 2022 consultation and immediate policy choices affecting 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Erdoğan because the statement ties the policy path to the government/central bank direction under his authority.
contrary_evidence: The IMF also noted a dynamic private sector and strong rebound from the pandemic.

evidence.claim: Erdoğan appointed Nureddin Nebati, a strong supporter of the low-interest-rate line, as treasury and finance minister, replacing the last top official seen to favor orthodox policy, and Reuters noted he had already fired three central bank governors since mid-2019.
evidence.title: Erdogan picks low-rates champion as finance minister as Turkish lira skids
evidence.excerpt: Erdoğan appointed Nureddin Nebati, a strong supporter of the low-interest-rate line, as treasury and finance minister, replacing the last top official seen to favor orthodox policy, and Reuters noted he had already fired three central bank governors since mid-2019.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters directly ties the appointment to Erdoğan's control over the economic team and describes the loyalty/orthodoxy pattern.
evidence.period_fit: Inherited into 2022 and still governing in the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: this is Erdoğan's appointment decision and part of his broader personnel control over economic policy.
contrary_evidence: Nebati had prior government experience as a deputy finance minister.
Appointment alone does not prove personal enrichment, only loyalty and policy alignment.

evidence.claim: The 2022 Presidential Annual Program set macroeconomic, fiscal, and sectoral policies around a strong and stable economy, competitive production, skilled people, liveable cities, sustainable environment, rule of law, democratization, and good governance, and said the measures would be monitored quarterly.
evidence.title: 2022 Yılı Cumhurbaşkanlığı Yıllık Programı 25/10/2021 Tarih ve 31639 (Mükerrer) Sayılı Resmi Gazete’de yayımlanmıştır
evidence.publisher: T.C. Cumhurbaşkanlığı Strateji ve Bütçe Başkanlığı
evidence.excerpt: The 2022 Presidential Annual Program set macroeconomic, fiscal, and sectoral policies around a strong and stable economy, competitive production, skilled people, liveable cities, sustainable environment, rule of law, democratization, and good governance, and said the measures would be monitored quarterly.
evidence.source_locator: official summary paragraph on the program page
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct government planning summary; reliable for the declared framework, but it is aspirational rather than proof of delivery.
evidence.period_fit: Adopted before and governing the 2022 calendar year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Formally attributable to Erdoğan's presidency and state apparatus; it shows the declared program, not personal authorship line by line.
contrary_evidence: A planning document does not itself show execution or course correction beyond the stated monitoring mechanism.

evidence.claim: The 2022 Investment Program, carrying Erdoğan's signature, allocated 184.3 billion TL to 3,134 projects and said priority went to projects with the highest economic and social impact and the most urgent service needs.
evidence.title: 2022 Yılı Yatırım Programı Yayımlandı
evidence.publisher: T.C. Cumhurbaşkanlığı Strateji ve Bütçe Başkanlığı
evidence.excerpt: The 2022 Investment Program, carrying Erdoğan's signature, allocated 184.3 billion TL to 3,134 projects and said priority went to projects with the highest economic and social impact and the most urgent service needs.
evidence.source_locator: paragraphs reporting the program and the total allocation
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct official investment-program announcement with explicit figures and signature attribution.
evidence.period_fit: This is the program for 2022 implementation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable at the formal executive level because the program is described as carrying Erdoğan's signature; completion still needs separate proof.
contrary_evidence: The allocation shows intent and prioritization, not that every project was completed on schedule.

evidence.claim: The 2022 Investment Program concentrated spending on transport and communications, education, energy, mining, agriculture, health, water and sewerage, and also funded major rail, metro, gas storage, flood control, wildfire, and dam projects.
evidence.title: 2022 Yılı Yatırım Programı Yayımlandı
evidence.publisher: T.C. Cumhurbaşkanlığı Strateji ve Bütçe Başkanlığı
evidence.excerpt: The 2022 Investment Program concentrated spending on transport and communications, education, energy, mining, agriculture, health, water and sewerage, and also funded major rail, metro, gas storage, flood control, wildfire, and dam projects.
evidence.source_locator: sector allocation and project examples in the body of the article
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct official sector allocation and project list; strong evidence of concrete prioritization, though not completion.
evidence.period_fit: 2022 budgetary execution plan and project list.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Erdoğan's government through the formal investment program; it shows what the administration chose to fund.
contrary_evidence: Sectoral allocations show priorities but do not by themselves prove delivery or impact.

evidence.claim: Türkiye's 2022-2024 Medium-Term Program set explicit targets for GDP growth, unemployment, inflation, exports, and tourism, and described the program as the tool that initiates the budget process and allocates resources in line with public policies and the Development Plan.
evidence.title: Türkiye Unveils 2022-2024 Medium-Term Program
evidence.excerpt: Türkiye's 2022-2024 Medium-Term Program set explicit targets for GDP growth, unemployment, inflation, exports, and tourism, and described the program as the tool that initiates the budget process and allocates resources in line with public policies and the Development Plan.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government investment-office summary of a formal program; good for stated goals and resource-allocation intent, not proof of implementation.
evidence.period_fit: Program adopted before 2022 and governing the period under review.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Co-developed by Treasury/Finance and the Strategy and Budget presidency under Erdoğan's administration; attribution is institutional rather than personal.
contrary_evidence: Targets later proved too optimistic on inflation, so the program is better evidence of intent than of realized control.

evidence.claim: Erdoğan publicly repeated that interest rates would keep falling and inflation would fall with them; Reuters framed this as part of an economic model engineered by Erdoğan amid a currency crisis.
evidence.title: Erdogan says interest rates will be lowered and inflation will fall too
evidence.excerpt: Erdoğan publicly repeated that interest rates would keep falling and inflation would fall with them; Reuters framed this as part of an economic model engineered by Erdoğan amid a currency crisis.
evidence.source_locator: article opening paragraphs and quoted remarks
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting is strong for the statement and context, while the policy attribution is still partly inferential.
evidence.period_fit: January 2022, squarely inside the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable because it quotes Erdoğan's public stance and links the policy line to his repeated intervention in monetary policy.
contrary_evidence: The article reports a claim and policy stance, not proof that the stance was economically sound or successfully implemented.

evidence.claim: Türkiye's government launched bank and bond-market measures to cool inflation and stabilise the currency while avoiding higher rates, and Reuters said the inflationary spiral followed central-bank cuts made under pressure from Erdoğan.
evidence.title: Turkey unveils latest salvo against soaring inflation
evidence.excerpt: Türkiye's government launched bank and bond-market measures to cool inflation and stabilise the currency while avoiding higher rates, and Reuters said the inflationary spiral followed central-bank cuts made under pressure from Erdoğan.
evidence.source_locator: article opening paragraphs and the section headed 'STEPS TAKEN'
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting with concrete policy details and explicit attribution to the low-rate line under Erdoğan.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable because the article ties the measures and earlier rate cuts to Erdoğan's policy preference and pressure.
contrary_evidence: Analysts quoted in the story argued the measures skirted the need to raise rates and might do little to control inflation.

evidence.claim: The Monetary Policy Committee cut the policy rate from 12 percent to 10.5 percent and said it would continue to use liraization, macroprudential tools, and data-driven decisions to support price stability, growth, and employment.
evidence.title: Press Release on Interest Rates (2022-42)
evidence.publisher: Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye
evidence.excerpt: The Monetary Policy Committee cut the policy rate from 12 percent to 10.5 percent and said it would continue to use liraization, macroprudential tools, and data-driven decisions to support price stability, growth, and employment.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary central-bank record of the decision and the stated policy framework; excellent for what was done, though not a direct presidential order record.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Formally a central-bank decision, but it aligns with and likely reflects Erdoğan's persistent low-rate line; attribution is moderate rather than absolute.
contrary_evidence: The central bank is formally independent, so the move is not identical to a personal presidential decree.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said Türkiye had made progress by rapidly increasing renewable energy production and expanding waste-treatment infrastructure, while noting that recent leadership announcements pointed to ambitious climate and resilience plans.
evidence.title: Financing the Next Generation of Green Growth and Prosperity in Turkey
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said Türkiye had made progress by rapidly increasing renewable energy production and expanding waste-treatment infrastructure, while noting that recent leadership announcements pointed to ambitious climate and resilience plans.
evidence.source_locator: highlight and summary paragraphs around lines 58-59 and 70-71
evidence.source_confidence_reason: High-quality World Bank summary of sector progress and leadership signals, though it is partly descriptive rather than audited outcome data.
evidence.period_fit: Published in 2022 and describing the 2022 policy environment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Leadership announcements are attributable to Erdoğan's administration, but the report does not claim he personally managed each project.
contrary_evidence: The report also says Türkiye remains resource-intensive and that more progress is still possible.

evidence.claim: President Erdoğan announced that exports reached a record 254.2 billion dollars in 2022, rose 12.9 percent year on year, and remained part of his stated goal of putting Türkiye among the world's top 10 exporters.
evidence.title: Türkiye's Exports Soar to Record USD 254 Billion in 2022
evidence.excerpt: President Erdoğan announced that exports reached a record 254.2 billion dollars in 2022, rose 12.9 percent year on year, and remained part of his stated goal of putting Türkiye among the world's top 10 exporters.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official announcement of the reported export figure and stated objective; reliable for the announced result, but causal credit is partly inferential.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective report on 2022 results, published immediately after the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable as a public announcement by Erdoğan, though the export outcome also reflects firms, exchange rates, and global demand.
contrary_evidence: Export growth was also shaped by external conditions and market dynamics, so the figure does not prove presidential competence by itself.

evidence.claim: Official Turkish statistics said annual GDP increased by 5.5 percent in 2022 and GDP per capita reached 10,659 US dollars at current prices.
evidence.title: Annual Gross Domestic Product - 2022
evidence.excerpt: Official Turkish statistics said annual GDP increased by 5.5 percent in 2022 and GDP per capita reached 10,659 US dollars at current prices.
evidence.source_locator: data-portal summary text in the search snippet
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official statistics are strong for the reported figures, though the page itself is surfaced through a search snippet because the portal is JavaScript-gated.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 outcome report, published after year-end.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Outcome data are attributable to Erdoğan's administration only in part; they also reflect tourism, private-sector activity, war shocks, and the post-pandemic rebound.
contrary_evidence: The same year also featured very high inflation and currency stress, so growth alone is not a clean competence proxy.

evidence.claim: Official Turkish statistics reported that unemployment fell to 10.4 percent in 2022, employment rose by 2.3 percentage points, and labour-force participation rose to 53.1 percent.
evidence.title: Labour Force Statistics - 2022
evidence.excerpt: Official Turkish statistics reported that unemployment fell to 10.4 percent in 2022, employment rose by 2.3 percentage points, and labour-force participation rose to 53.1 percent.
evidence.source_locator: data-portal summary text in the search snippet
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official labour-market statistics are strong for the reported outcomes, though causation remains shared with the private sector and broader macro conditions.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 outcome report, published after year-end.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the administration only in a broad sense, because employment responds to tourism, external demand, and the rebound from pandemic disruption.
contrary_evidence: These gains coexist with severe inflation and real-income erosion, so they do not prove broad policy success.

evidence.claim: The UN said more than 11.1 million tonnes of essential foodstuffs had been shipped under the Black Sea Grain Initiative, and it praised the role of Türkiye and President Erdoğan as the Istanbul channel became an important center for discreet diplomacy.
evidence.title: Black Sea Grain Initiative is renewed
evidence.excerpt: The UN said more than 11.1 million tonnes of essential foodstuffs had been shipped under the Black Sea Grain Initiative, and it praised the role of Türkiye and President Erdoğan as the Istanbul channel became an important center for discreet diplomacy.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The UN is a strong independent source for the existence and reported effects of the agreement and for the praise directed at Türkiye's role.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The mediation is attributable to Erdoğan and Türkiye at the diplomatic level, but it depended on Russia, Ukraine, and UN cooperation.
contrary_evidence: The agreement was multilateral and war-dependent, so Türkiye was necessary but not sufficient for the outcome.

evidence.claim: Ukraine's president thanked Erdoğan for the return of 215 Ukrainians after a prisoner exchange with Russia conducted thanks to Türkiye's mediation, and said five returned commanders would be under Erdoğan's close supervision in Türkiye.
evidence.title: Zelensky thanks President Erdoğan for the Exchange of 215 Ukrainians with Russia
evidence.publisher: Republic of Türkiye Directorate of Communications
evidence.excerpt: Ukraine's president thanked Erdoğan for the return of 215 Ukrainians after a prisoner exchange with Russia conducted thanks to Türkiye's mediation, and said five returned commanders would be under Erdoğan's close supervision in Türkiye.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official Turkish communication quoting and summarizing foreign counterpart thanks; good for the fact of mediation, but still not an independent audit of bargaining strength.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Erdoğan at the diplomatic level, though the swap also depended on Russian and Ukrainian decisions.
contrary_evidence: The exchange was a negotiated multilateral transaction, not a unilateral Turkish achievement.

unresolved_gaps: Direct 2022 nuclear-specific conduct is sparse; most positive evidence is alliance or humanitarian diplomacy rather than nuclear command, doctrine, or safety reform.
The package shows limited exposure and inherited NATO structure, but not a strong ruler-attributed improvement or deterioration in nuclear posture.

The package is strong on mediation and selective coercion, but weaker on independent verification of the civilian-harm allegations and on Erdoğan's own weighing of peaceful alternatives for the Syria/Iraq operations.
Several items are civic-space or press-repression evidence rather than direct physical-integrity harm, so the chapter partly relies on fear-climate inference.
Attribution for some harms is institutional rather than command-specific, especially for local policing and court actions.
There was no true 2022 succession or term-limit stress test, so the chapter relies on institutional erosion and media/election-law evidence instead of a direct transfer-of-power event.
Outcomes are heavily confounded by inflation shocks, external demand, the post-pandemic rebound, and CBRT formal independence, so causal credit remains partial.
Project-level delivery and regional/household distribution evidence are thinner than macro indicators.
The strongest welfare evidence is on health coverage and refugee cash transfers; housing, sanitation, and school-quality evidence is thinner.
Several positive items are donor-UNICEF/WHO partnerships, so Erdoğan attribution is meaningful but not exclusive.
There is no direct 2022 audited asset, gift, or procurement record for Erdoğan personally.
The strongest negative items are media-control and family-network allegations, not direct first-person dishonesty or self-dealing proof.
Project-level completion evidence is thin; the package shows allocation, program design, and some outcomes, but not audited delivery for specific 2022 initiatives.
Outcome attribution is still confounded by shocks and by private-sector behavior, especially on growth, exports, and labor-market statistics.
